specification.problem: Approximate a single-qubit unitary U to precision epsilon by a probabilistic protocol (PQF) over a universal gate set, modeled as an absorbing Markov chain whose transitions are multi-qubit unitaries followed by measurements, with finite termination and expected gate count log_b(1/eps)+O(log log(1/eps)).
specification.reconstruction_scope: Only the generic Markov-chain/expected-cost framework and the stated asymptotic gate-count scaling, plus a tiny assumed 3-state absorbing chain as illustration. Explicit PQF unitaries, measurement outcomes, fallback rules, and gate-set-specific constructions (Clifford+T, +V, +pi/12) and the definition of b are outside scope.

symbols.meaning: constant related to expansion property of the gate set
transition matrix of the Markov chain over states (unitaries up to fallback)
sub-stochastic transition block among transient states
expected gate cost of one transition from transient state i (assumed)
expected gate count of the protocol

equations.label: Expected gate count scaling
equations.description: Claimed expected gate count of the PQF decompositions.
equations.justification: Directly stated in the abstract for the three gate sets.
assumptions: b depends on the gate set; its value is not given

equations.label: Absorbing chain structure
equations.description: Canonical form of a Markov chain with absorbing states (target unitary absorbing).
equations.abstract_quote: implements a walk on a discrete Markov chain in which the target unitary is an absorbing state
equations.justification: Absorbing-state chain implies canonical block form; the actual state space is not specified.
assumptions: Transitions induced by unitary plus measurement are probabilistic

equations.label: Fundamental matrix
equations.description: Expected visits to transient states before absorption.
assumptions: spectral radius of Q is less than 1

equations.label: Expected cost
equations.description: Expected gate count from initial distribution pi over transient states with per-step costs c.
equations.justification: Generic cost accounting; the paper's cost model is not given.
assumptions: Initial distribution pi over transient states

equations.label: Finite termination
equations.description: Fallback ensures absorption in at most K steps, unlike RUS where Q^k only decays geometrically.
equations.abstract_quote: In contrast to RUS protocols, the presented PQF protocols terminate after a finite number of steps.
equations.justification: Finite termination implies the transient block is nilpotent (acyclic transient structure) if termination is certain.
assumptions: Termination holds with certainty, with fallback states counted as absorbing or leading to absorption

registers.name: data
registers.role: qubit holding the state to which U is applied

registers.name: ancilla
registers.role: extra qubits for multi-qubit unitaries followed by measurement

steps.description: Define the Markov chain with the target unitary as an absorbing state.
At each transient state apply a multi-qubit unitary from the gate set and measure ancillas; the outcome selects the next state (specific unitaries not given).
Fallback transitions guarantee absorption in a bounded number of steps.
Compute expected gate count via the fundamental matrix and compare to the stated scaling.

specification.measurement: Ancilla measurements after each multi-qubit unitary determine the transition; the measurement basis is not specified.
assumptions: Generic absorbing-chain formalism used as illustration
Cost model is additive per step
missing_information: Explicit state space and transition unitaries
Definition and values of b per gate set
Proofs of the scaling and constants
